items.title: 2024 Preliminary Draft Capital Budget Report
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report and noted a temporary increase of contributions from development charges over 3 years from 1.9 million to the following:
After a brief discussion, Council indicated support for the contribution increase from Development Charges to the capital budget by consensus.
Senior staff presenting the following capital projects in further detail and responded to questions from Council.
Plans and Studies
Active Transportation & Mobility Master Plan

The Master plan aims at establishing an active transportation network for the Township that considers the varied mobility needs of all residents and visitors. The Plan will take the Township’s existing network of sidewalks, trails, multi-use paths, and roads into consideration, and it will make recommendations for future improvements to enhance safety and connectivity. The Study will be completed in accordance with the Municipal Class Environmental Assessment process, and it will include public engagement and consultation.
Economic Development and Tourism strategic plan

A joint Economic Development and Tourism strategic plan will create a 20-year visionary plan to be able to create an intentional redirection of tourism strategies as sustainable drivers of economic development and build on existing and emerging economic development opportunities.
Parks and Recreation Master Plan and Parkland Strategy

The Parks and Recreation Master Plan identifies needs and priorities for the Township of Centre Wellington in the areas of parks, recreation facilities and recreation services. The current Plan was completed in 2018 and identified needs to the year 2028. Centre Wellington is facing unprecedented growth creating challenges to identify what will be needed to sustain current levels of service and meet the needs of a growing and diverse population. An update is needed to consider new challenges and opportunities. The update to the Plan would look at future growth targets forecasted 20-30 years into the future, and consider facilities, services and land recommendations to meet the community needs. The current challenge is how to strategically locate new facilities, parks and services as the community changes. This study will consider future needs and priorities, land and space needs, operational needs, growth targets, diversity, accessibility and provide the Township with a path forward. The methodology involves extensive research, consultation, and assessment efforts. Community and partner engagement will be part of the assessment and information gathering for the study.
Development Planning Policy

The Provincial government added land to the Fergus and Elora-Salem Urban Centre boundaries in its decision to approve County of Wellington OPA 119. Other lands may be added through the County Municipal Comprehensive Review (MCR) process and a number of property owners have requested the inclusion of their land. In order to ensure the logical and orderly progression of development, and the availability of municipal and community infrastructure, the Township needs to update its development policies and create a servicing allocation policy. This review will include an overview of municipal servicing, a review of the legislative authority for servicing allocation by-laws, leading to recommendations for the prioritization of development reflecting our local capacity constraints.
Jefferson Elora Community Centre (JECC) Asphalt Parking Lot The parking lot asphalt is at end of life and needs to be resurfaced.

Infrastructure will be coordinating this project as part of their asphalt program. This was intended as part of the JECC renovation project, however timing of the project requires performing this as a 2024 project, so it was excluded from the construction project. The work will be performed in August when sports are in the off season to allow for minimal interruption.
Jefferson Elora Community Centre Digital Sign

The current sign at the Community Centre is a manual sign that staff need to access with a ladder to change the messaging. This is a health and safety risk, time consuming, and antiquated for messaging. A new digital sign would improve messaging to promote Township programs and events. The project will take place in August at the same time as the parking lot paving so the power and fibre wire can be buried under the parking lot. The Township’s digital signs can all be hosted on the same software and updated from within the office.
Millburn Playground and Washroom

Millburn Park requires a new playground and washroom to augment the existing splashpad. Currently, there are portable washrooms onsite which are not ideal for small children at the splash pad. The addition of a washroom similar to the building at O’Brien Splash pad and a playground will enhance the variety and usability of the park. Utility servicing to the building site will be required to accommodate the addition of a washroom. This is a multi-year project and planning work is reflected in the 2024 capital budget.
Urban Forestry

The Township of Centre Wellington manages thousands of trees on streets, in parks, and in natural areas. The Centre Wellington Public Forest Policy captures the operation and management practices, procedures, policies, by-laws, and standards employed to protect and enhance the Township’s public forest. Centre Wellington aims to ensure healthy, vibrant, and sustainable practices to manage and maintain the public forest for generations to come.
Ainley Development – Required Offsite Improvements

To accommodate the Ainley development, offsite improvements are required to Gerrie Rd, Colborne St as well as a sanitary sewer extension through Drimmie Park. Work includes removal and replacement of approximately 825m of the existing road base/surface, hydro pole/hydro infrastructure relocations, installation of a new 300mm watermain and upgrading the west side to an urban standard including storm sewers, curb and gutter, multi-use path, street trees and streetlights. The east side will remain a rural standard.
Colborne St Reconstruction Design - John Street to Wilson Crescent Design work for the removal and replacement of approximately 415m of the existing road base/surface and the removal and

replacement/upsizing of approximately 220m of sanitary sewer to accommodate the projected flows being conveyed from the Ainley development. The remaining sanitary sewer along this section of Colborne St will also be removed and replaced.
East Mill Street Reconstruction

The East Mill Street reconstruction project is driven by the need to replace aging infrastructure in this area. The project also provides the opportunity to improve the aesthetics and function of the street and enhance access to downtown Elora. Phase 1 of the project is being carried out in 2023, and it includes the construction of most underground utilities. Phase 2 of the project will be completed in 2024, and this phase of work will focus on surface finishes such sidewalks and boulevards, decorative streetlights, street trees, seating, decorative features, final asphalt surface paving, and line painting.
Eighth Line W - Sideroad 11 to Wellington Rd 17

This segment of the Eighth Line W will be repaved to improve current road conditions. The project will also include drainage improvements such as ditching and culvert replacements. This segment of paved road was identified as a high-priority for replacement in the Township’s Asset Management Plan.
Fifth Line Bridge 4-E

Located on the Fifth Line between Wellington Road 22 and Sideroad 30 in former Eramosa Township, Bridge 4-E is key link between Centre Wellington and communities to the south. This project includes rehabilitation to the existing bridge deck and railing to improve safety and extend the life of the bridge.
First Line West Bridge 26-P

To improve safety, a guiderail system will be installed at Bridge 26-P, located on the First Line West just south of Sideroad 4 in former Pilkington Township. This project with also include drainage improvements and roadway erosion control measures.

Municipal Class EA for Closed Bridges 2-WG, 30-WG, 3-E, 5-E & 7-E The Township’s Bridge Program includes plans to review closed bridges, and where possible, re-open bridges to improve connectivity in rural areas. A key part of this process is the completion of Municipal Class Environmental Assessment studies to evaluate bridge options with public consultation and input. Options to be considered will include bridge removal without replacement, bridge rehabilitation and bridge replacement. Bridges 2-WG, 3-E, 5-E, and 7-E will be grouped into one study, and a separate study will be completed for Bridge 30-WG.
St David St N – St Andrew St to Edinburgh Ave

St David Street North is an important regional and local mobility corridor, economic hub for local business, and a gateway into Centre Wellington’s cultural and architectural heritage. As outlined in the Township’s Asset Management Plan, the road and buried infrastructure in this area is in urgent need of replacement. The Township has been selected for funding through the Ontario Ministry of Transportation's Connecting Links Program, with a contribution of $2,849,176 towards this project. The first phase of construction in 2024 will take place in the block from just north of the St. Andrew Street intersection to just north of the Garafraxa Street intersection. A second phase of construction will be completed in 2025, focusing on the block from Garafraxa St to Edinburgh Ave.
Bridge St Water Tower Exterior Overcoating

The interior and exterior coating is original and approximately 21 years old. In August 2022, a third-party assessment was completed on both the interior and exterior coatings. The results indicate that both interior and exterior coating are in fair condition, however an overcoat can increase the life cycle of the existing coating 10 to 12 years. If left as is, a recoat will be required in 2025. A full recoat would be well over $1,000,000. The exterior has substantial chalking and weathering of the lower cone, and the roof paint has completely deteriorated. The interior inspection indicates that there are number of corrosion spots where previous repairs have been made. This project will include an overcoat application to the exterior. Interior tank to be drained, cleaned and a touch-up coating to all corroded areas. Completing both external and internal projects brings efficiency to operations as well as cost savings.
The tower will also be updated with current Township branding.
Chalmers St Watermain Replacement

This project includes the replacement of approximately 145m of aged cast iron watermain with new PVC watermain on Chalmers St. from Moir St. to Colborne St, and the resurfacing of the road with new asphalt pavement. Road grades will also be reviewed to improve storm drainage where possible.
Fergus Waste Water Treatment Plant (WWTP) Biosolids Storage Assessment & Rehabilitation

The Fergus WWTP Biosolids Storage Assessment & Rehabilitation is required due to solids increasing and current storage is being maximized, sludge storage #3 roof has failed remediation steps and needs to be assessed. Primary digester roof showing signs of degradation.
Fergus Waste Water Treatment Plant (WWTP) UV System
Replacement

The WWTP requires an upgrade to the UV system due to increasing operation and maintenance costs. Existing equipment is 20 plus years old and components are no longer available or supported. UV light provides rapid, effective inactivation of microorganisms through a physical process. When microorganisms are exposed to germicidal wavelengths of UV light, they are instantaneously rendered incapable of reproducing and infecting. The process adds nothing to the water and UV light has no impact on the chemical composition or the dissolved oxygen content and does not create by-products.
Groundwater Model Updates, Wellhead Protection and Municipal Class EA Studies

The Township relies on municipal groundwater wells to supply water to residents and businesses. As outlined in the Township's 2019 Water Supply Master Plan, more water supply is needed for growth. This additional supply will come from a combination of optimizing production from existing water supply wells, and developing new municipal supply wells. An existing well located in Fergus (F2R), and two new well areas located in the rural areas surrounding Fergus and Elora (Area 7 and Area 3) are being studied to determine if they can be used for additional water supply. Part of the study and approval process includes using computer groundwater models to assess impacts caused by pumping from these locations. To ensure groundwater from these wells will be protected from drinking water threats, it is also necessary to delineate areas referred to as “Wellhead Protection Areas”.
Well F5 Treatment

Well F5 produces raw water which contains a high concentration of suspended solids (referred to as "turbidity"), caused by silt and sand particles in the water. The turbidity observed in raw water increases at higher pumping rates, so Well F5 is generally not pumped to the capacity permitted in the Township's Permit to Take Water. To increase the water supplied from Well F5 and improve treatment at this location, the Township will install a raw water filtration system capable of removing turbidity from raw water. This project includes the design, supply, installation, and commissioning of a turbidity treatment system at Well F5R.
Facilities
Corporate Operations Facility

The Township is in process of developing a new multi-department Operations Centre to be located at 965 Gartshore Street, Fergus. This facility will enable the Township to continue to effectively deliver services to meet the increasing needs of our growing community. The 2024 budget for this project will be used to fund earthworks and the installation of services at the development site. These works will pave the way for construction of the new facility, which is planned to begin in 2025.
Elora Tourism Washrooms

Redesigning the Elora Tourism Pocket Park will allow for seasonal washrooms to better serve the community and tourists in the core of Elora. The tourism peak season will often draw over 1000 visitors a day to the current indoor washrooms and Tourism Information desk. Tourism in Elora has grown to a point where it is necessary to include the pocket park in the plan to better serve visitors. Redesigning this space will give opportunities to serve after hours, reduce congestion in the Tourism Information Centre and utilize the pocket park as an extended space.

Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the entire preliminary 2024 capital budget and responded to questions regarding the Fergus Grand Theatre washroom renovation, audible pedestrian signals, accessible rubber mats, disc golf equipment, sidewalk repair and traffic calming measures.
He further provided an overview of the 3 Year Capital Forecast planned to form part of the 10 year capital plan.
